title: NY State Assembly · District 38
area: Queens: Ozone Park, Woodhaven, South Richmond Hill, and parts of Jamaica

context.text: No incumbent is on the November ballot: in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, David Orkin defeated incumbent Assembly Member Jenifer Rajkumar 58.8% to 40.9%, ending her bid for re-election. The Republican primary was canceled and Ruben Cruz II (R) advanced without appearing on the ballot.

summary.text: David Orkin is an immigrant workers'-rights attorney and union organizer who describes himself as a democratic socialist. He defeated incumbent Assembly Member Jenifer Rajkumar in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary and is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate in November. According to his campaign website, he is running on affordability, protecting immigrants from ICE and strengthening workers' rights.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia survey, Orkin's mother immigrated from Tijuana, Mexico, and his father's family has deep roots in the Jewish community in the U.S.; he says he spent two years organizing against the militarization of the Arizona-Mexico border and for humanitarian aid along the Mexico-Guatemala border.
Orkin holds a bachelor's degree from Vassar College (2013) and a law degree from CUNY School of Law (2022).
He says he helped found the Tucson chapter of Jewish Voice for Peace; the New York Jewish Week dates the chapter's founding to 2014 and reports that he remained involved with the group afterward.

He has worked as an immigrant workers'-rights attorney at Make the Road NY, where, in his words, he represented clients facing wage theft and employer abuse. Ballotpedia lists affiliations with Make the Road NY, UAW Local 2320 and the Democratic Socialists of America.

He is an elected member of the bargaining committee of his union, UAW Local 2320, where he says he helped negotiate a first contract that included raises of more than $10,000 for the lowest-paid staff, a free healthcare option, and a 35-hour workweek.

Orkin lives in Ridgewood. A campaign press release cited by the Queens Chronicle says he has organized in the immigrant rights movement for more than a decade, and that he launched his Assembly campaign on Jan. 7, challenging Rajkumar.

In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary he received 58.8% of the vote (3,722 votes) to Rajkumar's 40.9% (2,588); Rajkumar had represented the district since 2021. His campaign website lists endorsements including NYC-DSA, the New York Working Families Party and UAW Region 9A.
The New York Jewish Week reported that Orkin describes himself as an anti-Zionist Jew and that his platform centered on affordability and immigration.

priorities.text: "TAX THE RICH FOR AFFORDABILITY... As the richest New Yorkers and biggest corporations make more than ever, I'll fight for a state budget that asks them to pay their fair share in taxes to fund the services working people deserve: deeply affordable housing, universal childcare, guaranteed healthcare, fully funded public schools and free CUNY, world-class public transit, and more."

"PROTECT OUR IMMIGRANT NEIGHBORS. More than half of AD-38 residents are immigrants... In Albany, I'll fight to implement New York for All, ending collaboration between ICE & local law enforcement and protecting personal data from federal surveillance."

"STRENGTHEN WORKERS' RIGHTS... I'll champion the EmPIRE Worker Protection Act, which strengthens protections against wage theft, retaliation, unsafe workplaces, and union-busting. And I'll support a $30 minimum wage in New York."

summary.text: Ruben Cruz II is a small-business owner and community advocate who describes himself as the founding director of a health, wellness and arts programming firm. He is the Republican and Queens United Party candidate for Assembly District 38 and previously ran unsuccessfully for Assembly District 24 (2024) and State Senate District 16 (2022). According to his campaign website, he is running on protecting homeowners and seniors, rebuilding the local economy and cutting hidden fees.

background.text: Cruz graduated from Richmond Hill High School and holds a bachelor's degree in Theatre and Dance from CUNY Queens College (1999).
He says he is the founding director of a firm that has provided health, wellness, and arts and culture programming in New York City since 2006, and describes himself as a "Community Architect."

During the COVID-19 pandemic he founded the Queens Pet Pantry, a pet-supply distribution project; he says it was created in collaboration with city agencies and animal-welfare groups and that its data-management system was later adopted by the ASPCA. His campaign website says his team managed the Queens Pet Pantry and community-center relocations.
In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey he described working with the Community Agency for Senior Citizens on elder abuse and elder justice with the State Office of Victim Services.

He lives in Richmond Hill, Queens, and serves on Queens Community Board 9. Ballotpedia lists affiliations with the Latin American Intercultural Alliance, the Central Queens Republican Club and Queens Libertarians.
Cruz ran as the Republican, Conservative and Independence Party candidate for State Senate District 16 in 2022, losing to incumbent John Liu 57.7% to 42.2%.
In 2024 he ran as the Republican, Conservative and Common Sense Party candidate for Assembly District 24, losing to incumbent David Weprin 61.1% to 35.1%.
The 2026 Republican primary for Assembly District 38 was canceled and Cruz advanced to the general election on the Republican and Queens United Party lines.

priorities.text: On transit: "I will audit the MTA to bridge the... transit desert between Woodside and Woodhaven with reliable, eco-friendly bus service. We must address the alarming pollution levels in our subways to protect our health."

On homeowner protections: "I am fighting for economic justice for homeowners: I will legislate to ban property liens placed without owner knowledge and eliminate the hidden bank and utility fees that drain blue-collar paychecks."

On seniors and pets: "I am committed to preserving the rights of residents over 62 to live with their pets without housing discrimination and advocating for pet-friendly shelters so no neighbor is forced into homelessness to stay with a loved one."

researchNotes: Neither candidate has held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record for either. Orkin's positions are documented in depth from his campaign's detailed platform statements and Ballotpedia survey. Cruz completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey with extensive priorities in his own words, but did not take clear stances on this guide's fixed issue list, so no Position entries are included for him; his research depth is marked 'basic' accordingly. Biographies draw on candidates' own materials plus Ballotpedia and two news reports on Orkin; no news profile of Cruz II was found.
